name: Smoorsnoek
summary: Braised smoked snoek: flaked smoked fish folded into onions, potatoes and tomato with a little chilli, served on rice with apricot jam.
about: Smoor means to braise, and smoorsnoek is an old Cape dish that turns a single smoked snoek into a meal for a family. It is Cape Malay and West Coast home cooking, eaten with white rice and, in many homes, a spoon of apricot jam or chutney on the side.

ingredients.name: Smoked snoek
ingredients.note: about 350 g once skinned and boned

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.note: medium, peeled and cut into 1.5 cm cubes

steps: Skin the snoek and flake the flesh into bite-sized pieces, feeling carefully for bones with your fingers and removing every one.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the onions until soft and light golden, about 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes and fry, turning now and then, for 5 minutes, until the edges start to colour. Stir in the garlic and chilli and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and water, cover and simmer over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife. Add a splash of water if the pan goes dry.

Fold in the snoek gently, so it stays in flakes, and heat through uncovered for 5 minutes. It is ready when the fish is hot and the sauce clings to the potatoes. Taste before seasoning: smoked snoek is salty.
Finish with pepper, parsley and the lemon juice. Serve on white rice with apricot jam on the side.
